entities.summary: Radu D. Rosetti or Rossetti was a Romanian poet, playwright, and short story writer, also distinguished as an attorney and activist. The son of playwright-aristocrat Dimitrie Rosetti-Max and nephew of Titu Maiorescu, he had a troubled and rebellious youth, split between Romania and Austria-Hungary; during these debut years, he kept company with senior literary figures such as Ion Luca Caragiale and Alexandru Vlahuță. Graduating from the University of Bucharest at age 26, he was already a successful poet of neoromantic sensibilities, a published translator of plays and novels, and also famous for his unhappy marriage to the literary critic Elena Bacaloglu.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent figure in Romanian literature and activism, Radu D. Rosetti's work reflects the country's struggle for independence during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, influencing the development of neoromanticism and contributing to Romania's cultural identity.
